summary: A Yes vote enacts a City of Adelanto transactions and use (sales) tax.

tax.text: The Yes side supports a 1% transactions and use tax expected to raise about $3 million annually for streets, public safety, parks, homelessness response, and infrastructure.
tax.quote: paving streets and fixing potholes, fire protection, paramedic, and 911 response; law enforcement and crime prevention; keeping public areas/parks safe/clean; addressing homelessness; and repairing aging storm drains, pipes, bridges, and public areas by establishing a 1% transactions and use tax, providing approximately $3,000,000 annually until ended by voters, requiring audits, public spending disclosure, all money controlled locally, be adopted?

tax.text: The No position rejects Measure P’s proposed 1% sales tax for Adelanto city services.
tax.quote: A transactions tax is generally known as a sales tax. The sales tax is imposed on all retailers within the City of Adelanto at the rate of 1% (one percent) of the gross receipts of the retailer from the sale of all tangible personal property sold within the City.
